desc:
Connect AI to your own business data so it answers from your facts instead of guessing. Ecom Swift LLC links an assistant to your help articles, PDFs, product feeds, spreadsheets or database, cleans the content, keeps it fresh and shows the source behind each answer.

## What does it mean to connect AI to your data?

It means the AI reads your documents at the moment it answers a question, rather than relying on general knowledge from its training. When someone asks about your returns window or a product's materials, the system first finds the matching passages in your content, then writes the reply from those passages.

This approach is often called retrieval. It matters because a general model knows nothing about your prices, policies or stock, and it will often produce a confident answer anyway.

## Why unconnected AI gives wrong answers

An assistant with no access to your facts fills gaps with plausible text. A customer may be told a return period that does not exist, or a staff member may be given an outdated procedure. These errors are hard to spot because they read well.

Connected answers can be checked. When a reply shows which document it came from, a person can open that page and confirm it. That makes mistakes easier to find and fix at the source, which is usually a single out-of-date file.

## How good connections improve results

Accurate answers save support time, reduce back-and-forth with customers and let staff find internal information without asking a colleague. The effect depends on the quality of your content: clear, current documents give clear answers, while contradictory or stale ones give confusing replies.

Access rules matter too. Public visitors, staff and managers should not all see the same material. A connection that respects those boundaries lets you use private files without exposing them.

## What a good connection includes

- A list of sources, each with an owner who is responsible for keeping it current.
- Content clean-up that removes duplicates, broken formatting and out-of-date versions.
- Documents split into searchable pieces that keep their headings and context.
- Answers that name the document or page they came from.
- A scheduled refresh, so edits appear without a rebuild.
- Live lookups for fast-changing facts such as orders or stock, where the source allows it.
- Access rules by user group, so staff-only files stay private.
- A tested set of real questions with notes on what failed.
- An admin page where you can see which sources are connected.
- A written note on how to add or remove a source later.

## What we do

We start by mapping where your information lives and who may see it. We then read the content in, tidy it and split it for search. We test with real questions, fix gaps in the content or the settings and repeat until answers are reliable.

The Basic package connects one source with sourced answers. The Standard package handles several sources, a daily refresh and access rules by group. The Premium package adds live lookups, refresh on change where the source supports it, an admin view and a tuning call. Your data stays where it is unless you ask us to move it, and we tell you which services process it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Remove old policies and duplicate files before connecting them.
- Decide which groups may see which sources.
- Give each source a named owner.
- Test with the questions customers actually ask.
- Keep a short list of facts that must never be guessed, such as prices.

**Avoid:**
- Connecting private files to a public assistant.
- Letting two conflicting documents sit in the same source.
- Assuming the first test proves the system is ready.
- Uploading content you do not have the right to use.
- Leaving a source unmaintained after launch.

## Who it is for

A company with a long help center wants customers to get answers without searching it page by page. An online store wants an assistant that reads its product feed and shipping rules. A services firm has internal guides and wants staff to ask questions and see the original document.

## What we need from you

We need access to the sources you want connected, shared as a collaborator, viewer or developer user where the platform supports it, or as an export you send. We never need your passwords. Tell us which files are private and who may read them. A list of typical questions helps us test. After you order we send a short checklist and update you until the connection is live.
